problems.title: Number of Islands
problems.gist: You get an m x n grid of characters, each '1' (land) or '0' (water). Two land cells belong to the same island when they share a side: up, down, left or right (corners do not count). Assume everything outside the grid is water. Return the number of islands.

problems.title: Course Schedule II

gfg.t: A Valid Order to Complete Tasks

problems.gist: A training portal has numCourses modules, numbered 0 to numCourses - 1. You get a list prerequisites where each entry [a, b] means "module b must be finished before module a". Return an order in which you can finish all modules. If several orders work, return any of them.

problems.gist: You get an integer numLevels and an array rules, where rules[i] = [a, b] means level b must be completed before level a. Return true if it is possible to complete every level, otherwise false.

problems.title: Rotting Oranges
problems.gist: You get an m x n integer matrix shelf. Each cell is 0 (empty), 1 (good crate) or 2 (mouldy crate). Every minute, any good crate that is 4-directionally adjacent to a mouldy crate becomes mouldy.

problems.title: Clone Graph
problems.gist: A city's metro map is stored as an undirected, connected graph. Each station is a node with an integer val and a list neighbors of the stations it links to directly. You are handed a reference to one station.

problems.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
problems.gist: A courier network has n depots numbered 0 to n - 1. Each entry flights[i] = [from_i, to_i, price_i] is a one-way shipment link: it carries a parcel from depot from_i to depot to_i for price_i.

problems.title: Making A Large Island
problems.gist: A square map grid of side n holds 1 for land and 0 for sea. An island is a group of land cells joined through shared edges (up, down, left, right). You are allowed to reclaim at most one sea cell (turn one 0 into a 1).

problems.title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.gist: A rectangular island is split into an m x n grid of cells. You get the integer matrix heights, where heights[r][c] is the height of cell (r, c). The Pacific ocean touches the island's top and left edges; the Atlantic touches its bottom and right edges.

problems.title: Accounts Merge
problems.gist: You get a list accounts. Each element accounts[i] is a list of strings: accounts[i][0] is a name, and the rest are emails of that account.

problems.title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph

gfg.t: Connected Components in an Undirected Graph

problems.gist: A graph has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1. You are given the integer n and an array edges where edges[i] = [ai, bi] means there is an undirected edge between nodes ai and bi.

problems.title: Evaluate Division
problems.gist: You get a list equations where equations[i] = [A_i, B_i] and a matching list values, meaning A_i / B_i = values[i]. Each A_i or B_i is a string naming one variable.

problems.title: Flood Fill
problems.gist: An image is an m x n integer grid image, where image[i][j] is the colour of a pixel. You are also given a start pixel (sr, sc) and a colour color.

problems.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
problems.gist: You get an n x n grid grid of 0s (free) and 1s (blocked). Return the length of the shortest clear path from the top-left cell (0, 0) to the bottom-right cell (n - 1, n - 1), or -1 if there is none.
